captions.instagram:
How does a digital watch work?

No gears, no hands, no ticking. A sliver of quartz, a row of counters and a sandwich of liquid crystal that twists light keep the time on one coin cell for seven years. Take a digital watch apart in 3D and count the seconds yourself.

→ A digital watch has no gears and no hands: just a chip, a crystal, a coin cell and a piece of glass.
→ Take it apart: display glass, two rubber zebra strips, one chip under black epoxy, a 3 volt cell and a piezo beeper.
→ A quartz crystal hums 32,768 times a second. Fifteen flip-flops halve that beat down to exactly one tick a second.
→ One pulse a second feeds a row of counters. At 59 the seconds roll over and pass a carry to the minutes.
→ The date counter checks the month, and the year. In 2028, 28 February is followed by the 29th.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/digitalwatchclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a digital watch work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
No gears, no hands, no ticking. A sliver of quartz, a row of counters and a sandwich of liquid crystal that twists light keep the time on one coin cell for seven years. Take a digital watch apart in 3D and count the seconds yourself.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/digitalwatchclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/digitalwatchclear

In this video:
• A chip, a crystal, a cell and a piece of glass. Inside the resin case is a small module: a circuit board with one chip under a blob of black epoxy, a quartz crystal in a tiny can, and a 3 volt coin cell.
• One tick a second. The quartz crystal is cut like a tuning fork and rings 32,768 times a second.
• A row of counters. The chip does not know the time.
• Seven bars make every digit. Each digit is kept as four bits.
• A sandwich that twists light. A segment is liquid crystal between two polarisers set at right angles, over a reflector.
• Four jobs on a millionth of an amp. The Mode button steps the chip from clock to alarm to stopwatch to setting, and the other buttons change meaning in each.
